mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals robust residential construction and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic expansion supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where HOUST exceeds its 3-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE below 4.0%) and high federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS above 2.0%) indicates an overheating economy with tight labor markets and restrictive policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: The joint condition (UNRATE < 4.0% and FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) occurs but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals economic deceleration and reduced consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp during late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 100, it reflects strong manufacturing output and supply chain resilience, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate margins improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is above 100.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth level above 18500 billion dollars (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer and business spending support equity valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 exceeds 18500.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a 3-month federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals aggressive policy that dampens economic growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp during monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly employment level above 150,000 thousand persons (PAYEMS) indicates strong labor market conditions, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate hiring boost economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 150000.
